minutes.headline: Committee heard the first proposed FY23 budget and discussed pushing primary school air conditioning; no votes taken.
minutes.summary: The School Committee met remotely in a discussion-only session. It heard a safety team presentation, the first proposed FY23 school budget with new and cut positions, COVID testing options, and a goals update. A long discussion of primary school air conditioning and the town capital plan ended with two members agreeing to draft a letter to the town manager. The only vote was adjournment.

public_comment.stated_role: president of the Lunenburg Education Association
public_comment.topic: Urged action on air conditioning at the primary school and Turkey Hill, citing heat's effect on safety and learning.
Second public comment period; no hands seen. A member asked about kindergarten registration timing and was told it usually opens in February.

votes.outcome: passed by roll call; all five members voted aye

budget_items.what_was_said: Homeschooled students are not counted in the Chapter 70 formula; some are expected to return next year.
Chapter 70 has stagnated under the Student Opportunity Act and the FY23 amount has not been received.
Many ESSER and other COVID grants have been added; some positions will be reevaluated for sustainability as grants expire.
The proposed budget is a roughly 3 percent increase, split between personnel and non-personnel.
The budget includes an 8 percent insurance increase from the town manager, partly offset by school choice funding.
The proposed budget total was stated, along with new positions and a salary reserve.
figures_as_heard: two hundred and twelve thousand dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: The bid is out and the final amount will be known on February 17th.
About 65 percent of eligible expenses is expected back, with a possible adjustment for out-of-district transportation.
Several requested positions are tabled or moved to grant funding.

budget_items.topic: Out-of-district placement cost for a heat-related need
budget_items.what_was_said: A single placement driven by the lack of air conditioning could be costly.
A finance committee member said recent capital funding from free cash was record-level, and next year's free cash will likely be smaller.
A member computed the effect of declining enrollment on funding as small.

decisions.decision: The committee will keep meeting by Zoom through the February 2nd meeting.
The chair and Mr. Schoolambrini will form a subcommittee to draft a letter to the town manager, finance committee and select board about primary school air conditioning within about a week.
A strategy to help parents take part in capital planning and the air conditioning issue will be added to a future agenda, along with the transportation policy.
Budget question-and-answer periods were set for the February 2nd and March 2nd meetings, with the recommended budget on March 16th.

what_happened.line: The School Committee took no votes on the budget; the only vote was to adjourn, in a discussion-only remote session.
The committee heard the first proposed FY23 school budget, described as roughly a 3 percent increase, with new and cut positions and a salary reserve.
After a long discussion of primary school air conditioning and the town capital plan, two members agreed to draft a letter to the town manager, finance committee and select board.
Budget question-and-answer periods were set for February 2nd and March 2nd, with the recommended budget on March 16th.
The proposed budget includes an 8 percent health insurance increase, and the committee said the FY23 Chapter 70 amount had not yet been received.

why_it_matters: The FY23 school budget is the largest piece of what the town raises in taxes, and the final size depends on state aid not yet known, on grant-funded positions, and on insurance costs.
Primary school air conditioning competes for capital money in the town plan, so a letter to town boards could shape what residents are later asked to fund or vote on.
